The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is given above. Find $a$ and $b$ such that $f(x)\to a$ as $x\to \infty $ and $f(x)\to b$ as $x\to -\infty .$
question.worked_solution:
- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 2\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

Therefore, $a=2.$

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $-2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to -2\,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty 
$$

Therefore, $b=-2.$
